Edwards Responds to Ethics Committee Findings August 27, 2026 Press Release WASHINGTON, D.C. — Congressman Chuck Edwards sent a letter rebuking the House Ethics Committee's findings that he engaged in sexual harassment and outlining his concerns with the Committee's investigation and conclusions. In the letter, Edwards directly challenged the Committee's findings and provided his colleagues with his account of the allegations and the context surrounding the evidence and investigation. The Committee concluded that Representative Edwards did not violate federal sexual harassment law; concluded he engaged in no sexual activity with nor propositioned any staff member; and concluded that the allegations in the matter do not implicate quid pro quo sexual harassment. Yet the Committee used third-party testimony, omitted evidence, and made inferences that his conduct "could" be perceived as something the evidence itself failed to establish. "Sexual harassment is a serious offense. One that deserves to be defined clearly, investigated fairly, and established by evidence—not inference or speculation. I unequivocally reject the Ethics Committee's findings and its conclusion that I engaged in sexual harassment," said Congressman Edwards. "Those conclusions do not accurately reflect the facts or the full context surrounding these allegations. I sent this letter because every Member of Congress deserved to hear directly from me and have the opportunity to review the facts for themselves."   ###

Edwards Advances FY27 Agriculture Appropriations Bill June 5, 2026 Press Release WASHINGTON, D.C. — Congressman Edwards voted to pass H.R. 8646, the FY27 Agriculture, Rural Development, Food and Drug, Administration, and Related Agencies  to support rural America and strengthen farms across the nation. The FY27 Agriculture bill appropriates nearly $30 billion for the U.S. Department of Agriculture, Food and Drug Administration, and the Commodity Futures Trading Commission. The legislation supports programs that protect America’s food and drug supply, strengthen farmers and rural communities, and ensure families have access to critical nutrition programs.  Additionally, this legislation reins in unnecessary spending, refocuses agencies on their core missions, and puts the health, safety, and prosperity of American producers and consumers first. Congressman Edwards secured several key priorities for North Carolina’s 11th Congressional District in the FY27 Agriculture bill, including: $2,000,000  to Balsam Grove Volunteer Rescue for the construction of a new fire station. $1,500,000  to Henderson County EMS for the construction of a new EMS Substation in Henderson County. $3,000,000  to Mitchell County for the construction and development of the Resiliency Hub to strengthen disaster preparedness, response, and long-term recovery.  “Western North Carolina depends on strong farms, reliable emergency services, and resilient rural communities,”   said Congressman Edwards.  “This funding delivers critical investments that will support our farmers, strengthen disaster response and recovery efforts, and help our communities continue to grow and succeed.”                                              &nb

Edwards Announces Additional Helene Recovery Funding July 9, 2026 Press Release WASHINGTON, D.C.  — Congressman Chuck Edwards (NC-11) announced the release of more than $23 million in FEMA Public Assistance funds to support ongoing hurricane recovery efforts in North Carolina. Funding secured for Western North Carolina includes:   $2,504,272 to Mitchell County to repair park facilities along Cane Creek. $10,259,743 to North Carolina Emergency Management for emergency protective measures following Hurricane Helene. $933,168 to Henderson County for emergency protective measures following Hurricane Helene. $2,395,861 to the City of Asheville for disaster management costs following Hurricane Helene. $231,506 to Christmount Christian Assembly for road and retaining wall repairs following Hurricane Helene. $7,391,400 to North Carolina Emergency Management for debris removal operations. $236,098 to Haywood Electric Membership Corporation for disaster management costs following Hurricane Helene.   “Securing these funds is critical to finally moving from recovery to rebuilding,” said Congressman Edwards. “These resources allow us to get to work restoring our roads, rebuilding our bridges, and repairing the infrastructure Western North Carolina depends on every single day to keep communities connected and moving forward.”   Congressman Edwards has continued working with federal, state, and local officials to ensure Western North Carolina communities receive the resources needed to support long-term recovery and rebuilding efforts following Hurricane Helene.

Edwards Advances All 12 FY27 Appropriations Bills Through Committee June 25, 2026 Press Release WASHINGTON, D.C.  — Congressman Chuck Edwards (NC-11) announced the House Appropriations Committee has completed Fiscal Year 2027 markups, advancing all 12 annual appropriations bills out of committee. As a member of the House Appropriations Committee and Vice Chairman of the Subcommittee on National Security, Department of State, and Related Programs, Edwards worked to ensure taxpayer dollars are spent responsibly while advancing priorities that strengthen Western North Carolina and the nation. “I’m proud to bring Western North Carolina’s priorities to the table, especially as our mountain communities continue to rebuild after Hurricane Helene,”  said Congressman Edwards.  “Under Chairman Tom Cole’s leadership, we are delivering real results, supporting our communities, and ensuring Washington is accountable to taxpayers.” The FY27 appropriations bills fund key priorities including national defense, energy security, agriculture, rural development, and infrastructure improvements that support communities throughout NC-11. With committee work now complete, the FY27 appropriations bills will continue moving through the legislative process as Congress works toward final passage and the President’s signature. ###

Edwards Joins Chairman Bost to Introduce Take Care of America's Veterans Act | Congressman Chuck Edwards Skip to main content 1505 Longworth House Office Building, Washington, DC 20515 Email Me (202) 225-6401 X How Can I Help? Edwards Joins Chairman Bost to Introduce Take Care of America's Veterans Act June 23, 2026 Press Release WASHINGTON, D.C. — Congressman Chuck Edwards (NC-11) joined House Veterans’ Affairs Committee Chairman Mike Bost (IL-12) to introduce the  Take Care of America’s Veterans Act , comprehensive legislation to improve veterans’ access to care, strengthen benefits, and modernize VA services. The package includes reforms to expand health care access, improve mental health and suicide prevention programs, support caregivers and surviving military families, modernize disability claims processing, and strengthen accountability across the VA system.  It also includes the Major Richard Star Act to ensure combat-disabled medically retired servicemembers can receive both military retirement pay and VA disability benefits without offset. “Our veterans deserve a VA system that works for them,”   said Congressman Edwards . “This legislation improves access to care, strengthens benefits, modernizes outdated systems, and ensures taxpayer dollars are being used responsibly. I’ll continue working to make sure that every veteran in Western North Carolina receives the support and services they’ve earned through their sacrifice and service.” ###

Edwards Advances FY27 National Security and State Department Funding Bill July 15, 2026 Press Release WASHINGTON, D.C. — Congressman Edwards voted to pass the FY27 National Security, Department of State, and Related Programs Appropriations Bill to strengthen America's national security and support key allies. The FY27 National Security and State Department bill strengthens America's position abroad by supporting key allies like Israel, Taiwan, Jordan, and Egypt while confronting threats from Communist China, Iran, drug cartels, and other adversaries. The legislation refocuses foreign assistance on advancing U.S. national security and economic interests, while ensuring our international partners do their fair share. Additionally, the bill cuts wasteful spending, increases oversight of foreign assistance programs, and ensures taxpayer dollars are spent on policies and programs that make America safer, stronger, and more prosperous. As Vice Chairman of the House Appropriations Subcommittee on National Security, Department of State, and Related Programs, Congressman Edwards played a key role in advancing the legislation through the appropriations process. " America's foreign policy should put the interests of the American people first,”  said Congressman Edwards. “This bill strengthens our national security, supports our allies, counters our adversaries, and ensures taxpayer dollars are spent responsibly. As Vice Chairman of the National Security and State Department Appropriations Subcommittee, I'm proud to help advance legislation that reinforces America's leadership abroad while demanding greater accountability for every dollar we spend.” ###

Edwards Advances More Than $25 Million for Western North Carolina in FY27 Appropriations Season June 29, 2026 Press Release WASHINGTON, D.C.  — Congressman Chuck Edwards (NC-11) has voted to advance all 12 annual federal spending bills through the House Appropriations Committee this year, securing more than $25 million in targeted investments for communities across Western North Carolina. Federal appropriations bills fund the day-to-day operations of the U.S. government and must be approved each fiscal year. While the legislation must still pass both the House and Senate before being signed into law, committee approval marks a significant step forward in the funding process. "As the only North Carolina appropriator, I work to ensure Western North Carolina receives critical federal investment. These bills will address local needs today and build a stronger future for generations to come,”  said Congressman Edwards.
